All Lie groups and Lie algebras are taken to be finite-dimensional.

::: Definition
[]{#LCM label="LCM"} A crossed module ${\Gc= ( \d\colon E \to  G,\tr)}$ is given by a group morphism $\d\colon E \to G$ together with a left action $\tr$ of $G$ on $E$ by automorphisms, such that:

1.  $\d(X \tr e)=X \d(e)X^{-1}; \forall X \in G, \forall e \in E,$

2.  $\d(e) \tr f=efe^{-1};\forall e,f  \in E.$

If both $G$ and $E$ are Lie groups, $\d\colon E \to G$ is a smooth morphism, and the left action of $G$ on $E$ is smooth then $\Gc$ will be called a Lie crossed module.

blocks.title: Crossed modules and categorical groups
blocks.content:
[]{#CCG label="CCG"}

::: Definition
A categorical group $\mathcal{C}$ is a groupoid provided with a strict monoidal structure $\C \times \C \ra{\tn} \C$, as well as a "group inversion" functor ${^{-1}}\colon C  \to C$ such that both the set of objects $C_0$ of $\C$ and the set of morphisms $C_1$ of $\C$ are groups under the tensor product, and both the source and target maps $\sigma,\tau \colon C_1 \to C_0$ are group morphisms. A Lie categorical group is defined analogously by replacing groups by Lie groups and group morphisms by Lie group morphisms.
:::

See [@BM; @BL] for more details.

:::

::: Definition
[]{#thin2 label="thin2"}

Two 2-paths $\G$ and $\G'$ are said to be rank-2 homotopic (and we write $\G\cong_2 \G'$) if there exists a smooth map ${J}\colon [0,1]^2 \times [0,1] \to M$ such that:

1.  $J(t,s,0)=\G(t,s),\, J(t,s,1)=\G'(t,s)$ for $s,t\in [0,1]$.

2.  ${J}$ is constant over $\{0\} \times [0,1]^2$ and $\{1\} \times [0,1]^2$.

3.  Over $[0,1] \times \{0\} \times [0,1]$ the map ${J} \colon [0,1]^2 \times [0,1] \to M$ restricts to a rank-1 homotopy $\d_d(\G) \to \d_d(\G')$.

[]{#TCM label="TCM"}

Since $\Sc_2(M)$ is a 2-category, given a base point $*$ of $M$ (in other words an object of $\Sc_2(M)$) we can define a monoidal category $\Pc_2(M,*)$. The objects of $\Pc_2(M,*)$ are given by all 1-tracks of $M$ starting and ending at $*$, and therefore by all elements of $\pi_1^1(M,*)$. Recall the definition of the curvature 2-form $\W$ of a connection 1-form $\w$ as the covariant exterior derivative of the 1-form $\w$.

::: Definition
Let ${\Gc=(\d\colon E \to G,\tr)}$ be a Lie crossed module, and let $P \to  M$ be a smooth principal $G$-bundle. The 2-curvature 3-form of a $\Gc$-categorical connection $(\w,m)$ on $P$ is defined as $$\M=d m\circ(H \times H \times H).$$ In other words: $$\M(A,B,C)=dm(A^H,B^H,C^H),$$ where $A,B,C \in \X(P)$ are smooth vector fields on $P$.

blocks.title: The 2-structure equation
blocks.content:
[]{#se label="se"} The following equation is an analogue of Cartan's structure equation. It will be of prime importance later.

::: Proposition
Let ${\Gc= ( \d\colon E \to  G,\tr)}$ be a Lie crossed module. Let $P$ be a principal $G$-bundle over the manifold $M$. Let also $(\w,m)$ be a categorical $\Gc$-connection on $P$. We have: $\M=dm {+}\w\wedge^\tr m,$ where $\M=D m$ is the 2-curvature $3$-form of $(\w,m)$. In particular the 2-curvature 3-form $\M$ is $G$-equivariant, in other words: $R_g^*(\M)=g^{-1} \tr \M,$ for each $g \in G$.
:::

blocks.title: The 2-Bianchi identity
blocks.content:
Fix a Lie crossed module ${\Gc= ( \d\colon E \to  G,\tr)}$. Let $P$ be a smooth principal $G$-bundle over $M$ with a connection $\w$. Choose a $\Gc$-categorical connection $(\w,m)$ on $P$.

::: Proposition
Let $\M\in \A^3(P,\le)$ be the 2-curvature 3-form of $(\w,m)$. Then the exterior covariant derivative $D \M$ of $M$ vanishes. In other words: $$d \M \circ (H \times H \times H \times H)=0,$$ which by lemma [\[ext\]](#ext){reference-type="ref" reference="ext"} is the same as: $$d \M +\w \wedge^{\tr} \M=0.$$
:::

blocks.title: Definition of a holonomy.
blocks.content:
The following definition appears in [@CP].

::: Definition
Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds. Suppose that $M$ has a chosen base point $*$. A map $F \colon \pi_1^1(M,*) \to N$ is said to be smooth if, for any $2$-path $\G\colon [0,1]^2 \to M,$ with $\d_l(\G)=\d_r(\G)=*$, the map $$s \in [0,1] \mapsto F([\g_s])\in N$$ is smooth. Here $\G(t,s)=\g_s(t)$, where $s,t \in [0,1]$.

Let $G$ be a Lie group. A holonomy is, by definition, a smooth group morphism $\pi_1^1(M,*) \to G$.
:::

::: Definition
[]{#K label="K"} Let $M$ be a manifold. A smooth map $J \colon[0,1]^3\to M$, say $J(t,s,x)=\G^x(t,s)=\g^x_s(t),$ where $t,s,x \in [0,1]$, is said to be a 3-path if:

1.  $J$ is constant over $\{0\} \times [0,1]^2$ and over $\{1\} \times [0,1]^2$.

2.  $J$ restricts to a rank-1 homotopy (connecting $\g^0_0$ with $\g^1_0$) over $[0,1] \times \{0\} \times [0,1]$ and over $[0,1] \times \{1\} \times [0,1]$ (connecting $\g^0_1$ with $\g^1_1$).

3.  $J$ has a product structure close to the boundary of $[0,1]^3$; see definition [\[thin2\]](#thin2){reference-type="ref" reference="thin2"}
